key_insight: PedDx classified pediatric posterior fossa tumors from T2-weighted MRI, with higher accuracy among cases retained after confidence-based abstention.
clinical_relevance: The framework could support diagnostic assessment, but confident errors and imaging vulnerabilities limit readiness for routine clinical use.
method: Agentic workflow for independently generated predictions and structured quality-control reports.
evidence_signal: Evaluation included 492 discovery, 114 replication, 129 external validation, 40 independently tested, and 236 out-of-distribution cases; accuracy rose from 79.8% to 90.5% in replication, 81.4% to 88.7% in external validation, and 92.5% to 97.3% in independent testing when restricted to non-abstained cases.
watch_item: Out-of-distribution cases produced confidently incorrect predictions, and imaging perturbations exposed acquisition and alignment vulnerabilities; higher non-abstained accuracy does not represent all-case performance.
paper_title: PedDx: An End-to-End Deep Learning Framework for Pediatric Posterior Fossa Tumor Diagnosis with Agentic AI-Enabled Independent External Evaluation
